vars.team_intro: For significant features or changes that are more than a few lines of code, run a structured multi-agent workflow. You are the lead: start each role with `spawn_agent`, using the type, `model_config_id` and `reasoning_effort` from the role roster below. In its prompt, tell the child it is not the lead and to call `read_skill` with its role skill first, then give it the task as a complete prompt, because a child starts with no history of this chat. Use `wait_agent` to finish a step before starting the next. Only you can spawn roles: a child cannot spawn another and cannot ask the human, so relay its questions in this chat.
vars.worktree_section:
**All agents share one workspace dir.** Before starting any agent, create it and the feature branch (below). Every spawned agent shares this chat's workspace machine, so give each one the absolute path of the workspace dir and of each repo clone in its prompt; each agent edits code inside the clone, and the workflow artifacts stay in the workspace dir.

**Where work lives.** Only `~/work` (`/home/coder/work`) survives a workspace stop; everything else under the home directory, such as `~/skim`, is erased whenever the workspace stops. Clone every repo into `~/work`, and keep the workspace dir there too. After the first commit on a branch, push it, and push after every commit, so no work exists only in the workspace. When the work is done and reviewed, open a PR with `gh pr create`, linking the issue if there is one: a normal PR, ready for review. Exception: before pushing a security fix, or work on a vulnerability the security review finds, check the repo's visibility with `gh repo view <owner/name> --json visibility`. If it isn't PRIVATE (public, internal, or the check fails), treat it as public. Public: never push it. Commit it on a local branch under ~/work and stop for the human. If the security review finds a vulnerability after the branch is pushed, stop pushing, keep the details only in the workspace (never in the PR, commit messages or chat-visible links), and tell the human in the chat. Private: the normal PR flow applies, but don't describe the vulnerability in the PR title or description beyond what's needed, and tell the human in the chat.
vars.role_files: Role definitions are the skills `role-<role>` in `~/.coder/skills/`, which a spawned child reads with `read_skill`. Coder keeps the first skill of each name it finds and scans `~/.coder` before the project, so a project cannot override a role, and a project skill with the same name as one of ours (such as `tdd` or `grilling`) is silently dropped. Give project skills other names.
vars.child_guard: **If you were told to read a `role-*` skill, you are that role and not the lead.** Follow that skill and the task you were given. Do not start agents, create a workspace dir, propose a variant or ask the human anything; the sections below are for the lead. Return your report as your final message.
vars.design_review: Post the doc in the chat so the human can read it there, and wait. The architect revises from the human's comments in the chat. The human approves by replying `approve design` in the chat.
vars.human_gate: **Open the PR.** Put the description on the PR with `gh pr edit --body-file <file>`, make sure it is ready for review (a normal PR, never a draft), request a review from the human with `gh pr edit --add-reviewer "$TEAM_REVIEWER"` (the image sets `TEAM_REVIEWER` to their GitHub login; if it is unset, ask for the login in the chat), and say in one line in the chat that it is ready for review, linking it.
vars.ship: Every commit is pushed (see Where work lives). You cannot merge: branch rulesets leave that to the human. Commits here are unsigned: say so in the PR description.
vars.first_push: No push needs approval from the human, and the PR is ready for review from the moment it opens. Push after every commit (a security fix on a public repo is never pushed; see Where work lives), and push each fix
vars.security_stop: follows the rule in Where work lives: on a public repo it is never pushed and the details stay in the workspace; on a private repo the normal PR flow applies without describing the vulnerability. Either way, tell the human in the chat.
vars.workspaces_intro: Every task that needs a branch gets a **workspace**: a plain directory at `~/work/.workflow/<feature>/`, under `~/work` so it survives a workspace stop. It is not a git repo and needs no tool. It holds the agents' working files (`design.md`, `tests.md`, `followups.md`, review reports, `review-guide.md`). The repos are ordinary clones under `~/work/<repo>`. Working files stay in the workspace dir and **never go in a project repo**. Only the project's own code, tests and user-facing docs do.
vars.workspace_commands:
- Create the workspace dir with `mkdir -p ~/work/.workflow/<feature>`. In each repo the feature touches, pull the default branch and start the feature branch with `git switch -c feat/<feature>`.
- When the PR is merged there is nothing to close: the workspace dir is a plain folder, so delete it only if the human asks.
vars.workspace_locate: your prompt gives its absolute path
vars.engineer_checkout: You work in the clone of the repo you're changing, `~/work/<repo>`, on the feature branch the lead started; your prompt gives the path. Working files stay in the workspace dir and never go in the project repo. Commit in each repo separately.
vars.close_workspace: Clean up: after the human merges, the workspace dir is a plain folder under `~/work` and needs no command. Delete it only if the human asks.
vars.workspace_where: the workspace dir (your prompt gives its absolute path)
vars.workspace_fallback: If your prompt gave no workspace dir, use `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` instead, never the working tree.
